mobile.label: Mobile
preconditions: A physical device or emulator is available on a supported OS version.
The latest build of the app is installed and launched for the first time.
The test account is logged in and network connectivity is stable.
mobile.launchStep: Launch the app on the target device and wait for the home screen to load.
checks: Confirm the component renders correctly in both portrait and landscape orientation.
Confirm touch targets are at least 44x44 points and respond to a single tap.

web.label: Web
preconditions: The application is deployed to the target environment and reachable.
A supported browser is open with cache and cookies cleared.
The test account has the permissions needed to reach the component.
web.launchStep: Open the application URL in a supported browser and sign in as the test user.
checks: Confirm the component is reachable by keyboard navigation and exposes an accessible name.
Confirm the layout holds at 1920px, 1366px and 375px viewport widths.

desktop.label: Desktop
preconditions: The desktop client is installed on a supported OS build.
The application is started from a clean user profile.
The test account is signed in with default preferences applied.
desktop.launchStep: Start the desktop client and wait for the main window to finish loading.
checks: Confirm the component behaves correctly when the window is resized and maximised.
Confirm the documented keyboard shortcuts and focus order work as specified.

tablet.label: Tablet
preconditions: A tablet or tablet emulator is available on a supported OS version.
The latest build is installed and the app has completed first-run setup.
The test account is logged in with the default workspace selected.
tablet.launchStep: Open the app on the tablet and wait for the primary screen to settle.
checks: Confirm split-view and multi-window layouts render without clipping.
Confirm the component responds to both touch and an attached keyboard.

api.label: API
preconditions: The service is deployed to the target environment and the base URL is known.
A valid API credential with the required scope is available.
Test data fixtures are seeded and the database is in a known state.
api.launchStep: Authenticate against the service and confirm a 200 from the health endpoint.
checks: Confirm the response schema matches the published contract, including field types.
Confirm the status code, content-type and any pagination headers are correct.

smoke.label: Smoke
smoke.description: Critical path only — does the component work at all?
assertions: The component loads without error and the primary action completes.

regression.label: Regression
assertions: No console errors, crashes, or unhandled exceptions are produced during the run.

negative.label: Negative
assertions: The failure is surfaced to the user in plain language, not a raw error code.
The component recovers to a usable state once the failure is dismissed.

boundary.label: Boundary
boundary.description: Limits, empty states and overlong input.
extraSteps: Repeat the action with the minimum permitted value, then the maximum permitted value.
Repeat the action with an empty value and with a value one character over the limit.
assertions: Values at the minimum and maximum limits are accepted without truncation.
Values beyond the limit are rejected before submission, with the limit stated.
Empty input is rejected without discarding the rest of the form.

negativeVariants.label: invalid input
negativeVariants.stepSuffix: using invalid data that fails validation
assertions: A validation message identifies the offending field and states what is required.
The action is not submitted and no partial state is persisted.

negativeVariants.label: interrupted
negativeVariants.stepSuffix: then cancel or navigate away before the action completes
assertions: The in-flight action is abandoned cleanly with no orphaned record created.
Returning to the component shows the pre-action state, not a stale loading indicator.

negativeVariants.label: backend failure
negativeVariants.stepSuffix: while the backend is returning an error or is unreachable
assertions: The failure is reported without losing the data the user already entered.
A retry is offered and succeeds once the backend recovers.
